name: Adaptive music
what: A whole adaptive soundtrack synthesised live with Web Audio, no files: electric piano, synth bass, clav, a sax-like lead, strings, vibes and a jazz kit with reverb, delay and tape wobble. A lookahead scheduler and a small conductor follow the game: intensity fills in the drums, danger switches to a tension vamp, progress and checkpoints move through an arc of sections, airtime opens the sound up, pickups play stingers in key, a win resolves into an outro and a loss tape-stops into silence.
use_when: the game wants music that reacts to speed, danger or progress without shipping audio files or paying for generated tracks
good_for: Racing, rolling, flying or runner games with a run that has a beginning, rising stakes and an end; relaxed or golden-hour moods; any game that wants music answering the player without audio files.
not_for: Horror, epic orchestral, chiptune or any style far from jazz fusion (the engine can be reused but the progressions, melodies and patches must be rewritten); games that need identical music every run (it humanises with Math.random). Nobody has confirmed by ear that it sounds good: a person must listen before shipping.
